rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this iteration pushes obfuscation upward while respecting that objinst is a tiny (634-byte text, 9-function) but runtime-hot OOP benchmark whose Toggle/NthToggle methods sit inside million-iteration loops. SUB, FLA, and SPLIT get the highest security/diversity weights because they are structurally cheap and compose well — SPLIT enlarges basic blocks so FLA's dispatcher and BCF's bogus regions have more material to obscure in this very small code footprint. ICALL and IGV are raised moderately to virtualize method dispatch (methcall/objinst are call-centric) and obscure the object/hash state globals, since correctness held last round. BCF is deliberately kept mid-range: its bogus-region cloning gives the worst size blowup relative to this minuscule binary and its opaque predicates are the main runtime tax in the hot toggle loops, so a ~0.5 cost weight lets the selector apply it only where the dispatcher loop (main) justifies it. IBR stays moderate to diversify control flow without compounding BCF's loop overhead. All CorrectnessRisk weights remain below 0.3 since the previous table showed clean compilation and execution, indicating headroom for slightly more aggressive transformation rather than retrenchment.
